title: Changing package managers doesn't remove your npm registry dependency
partialText: npm is both a command and a package registry. Learn what switching to pnpm or Bun changes, and how caches, lockfiles, and mirrors affect failed installs.

title: OpenCode Code Mode explained: JavaScript instead of repeated tool calls
partialText: Learn how OpenCode Code Mode combines tool calls in JavaScript, when batching helps, and where permissions, errors, and side effects still need care.

title: MCP server design: tools, authentication, and rate limits
partialText: How to design a useful MCP interface for your product, with clear tools, account permissions, usage limits, predictable results, and safe writes.

title: Selling SaaS to developers: how to find paying customers
partialText: Developers can build alternatives to your product. That doesn't make them bad customers. Look at urgency, budgets, and the work buying lets them avoid.

title: How to build agents that survive crashes with Pi Durable
partialText: Build a durable TypeScript agent with Pi Durable and SQLite. Test crash recovery, avoid duplicate requests, and understand which tools can safely run again.

title: A deep dive into OpenSEO
partialText: Explore OpenSEO's architecture: SEO data APIs, Cloudflare Workers, its audit crawler, MCP tools, AI agents, storage, and self-hosting trade-offs.

title: How to write an OpenCode plugin with the v2 API
partialText: Build your first OpenCode v2 plugin in TypeScript, register a custom tool, validate its inputs, test the logic, and understand how v1 plugins change.

title: Build vs buy software: when AI can replace a SaaS
partialText: AI changes the build-versus-buy calculation, but a working prototype is only part of it. How to compare ownership, maintenance, risk, and recurring costs.

title: How to compete with AI-generated SaaS clones
partialText: Cheap software clones change what a small SaaS business can charge for. A practical look at differentiation, maintenance, distribution, and earning trust.

title: Meta released Muse Spark Open: what you can run, and what it takes
partialText: Meta released Muse Spark Open with downloadable weights, a million-token context, and support for coding agents. Here are the hardware and license limits.

title: The complete guide to Void: full-stack Vite apps with Hono and Cloudflare
partialText: Build and deploy full-stack Vite apps with Void, Hono, React, and Cloudflare D1. Learn typed routes, forms, migrations, authentication, and team hosting.

title: How to use OpenCode
partialText: Learn how to install OpenCode, connect a model, make your first code change, and configure project instructions and permissions in this hands-on tutorial.

title: What “open weights” means for AI models
partialText: Learn what open weights means for AI models, how it differs from open source, and what the Qwen3.8 and Kimi K3 downloads show about licenses and scale.

title: How to handle web requests in C with CGI 1.1
partialText: Learn CGI 1.1 by building a C web application: read requests, decode forms, return HTML and errors, and run the executable through Apache.

title: A deep dive into LangChain and LangGraph
partialText: Learn LangChain and LangGraph with TypeScript: models, prompts, tools, agents, memory, streaming, RAG, graphs, persistence, and human approval.

title: How I fixed a full Ubuntu server disk with Codex
partialText: My Sendy server stopped responding with the disk at 99%. The database was 528 MB, but MySQL binary logs had grown to 41 GB. Here is how Codex walked me through finding them, purging them safely, and setting an expiry so it never happens again.

title: How to create an Apple TV app
partialText: Build a tvOS app with SwiftUI, share code with your Mac app, design it for the Siri Remote, make its layered icon, and install it on your own Apple TV.

title: How to install your own apps on your iPhone with Xcode
partialText: Put the apps you build on your iPhone without the App Store: turn on Developer Mode, install from Xcode, update over Wi-Fi from the terminal, and renew them.

title: How to use Jev with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
partialText: How to use Jev with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor: install TypeSafe's agent skill, give the agent the docs, and review the Jev code it writes.

title: The complete guide to LiveKit Agents
partialText: Build a voice AI agent with LiveKit Agents in Node.js and TypeScript, then test it, simulate calls, deploy it to LiveKit Cloud and watch real sessions.

title: How to compile JavaScript into a single executable
partialText: Turn a JavaScript program into one executable file, like Go and Rust do, with deno compile, bun build --compile and Node.js single executable apps.

title: Use WhatCable to figure out what your USB cable can do
partialText: WhatCable is a free, open source Mac app that reads the chip inside a USB-C cable and tells you its real data speed, power rating and what limits it.

title: How to avoid the "Open Anyway" message when building macOS apps
partialText: macOS blocks apps downloaded from the internet until people click Open Anyway. Sign your app with a Developer ID and notarize it, and it opens normally.

title: What happens when AI agents shop for us
partialText: Shopify wants Muse to check out with Shop Pay on every store. I want the agent to find the product. I still want a person to approve the exact charge.

title: Use npkill to find and delete old node_modules folders
partialText: npkill is a free terminal tool that finds every node_modules folder on your computer, shows its size and age, and deletes the ones you pick.

title: I built Repo Foyer, a Chrome extension that puts my repos on the GitHub home page
partialText: Repo Foyer is my free, open source Chrome extension that replaces the GitHub home page with your repositories, so you can jump to the one you're working on.

title: I open sourced testvm, so your coding agents can test Mac apps in a VM
partialText: testvm is my free, open source tool that runs Mac app builds in a headless macOS VM, so coding agents test them without taking over your screen.

title: I built Footage Ferry, a Mac app to import Blackmagic Camera videos
partialText: Footage Ferry is my free, open source Mac app that copies Blackmagic Camera clips from an iPhone over USB, checks every copy byte for byte, and then offers to delete the originals.

title: How to use Jev with the Vercel AI SDK
partialText: How to use Jev with the Vercel AI SDK: install the TypeSafe provider, call experimental_evaluate, read confidence, use AI Gateway, and compare Jev with an LLM.

title: I built Chip Pops, 6,000 8-bit sound effects for my apps
partialText: Chip Pops is my free, open source Mac app and command line tool with about 6,000 8-bit sound effects made with jsfxr. Click a sound to hear it, drag it into your app.
